This course is for people who know JavaScript or C/C++ but have never written a shader. Every lesson shows a live picture on the left and the code that draws it on the right: drag any number in the code, or edit the code itself.

- 01 Fragments and data

- 02 Drawing shapes with math

- 03 Time, interaction and repetition

- 04 Textures and noise

- 05 Data becomes vertices

- 06 Space, camera and depth

- 07 Surfaces and light

- 08 What Three.js writes for you

- 09 Drawing in several passes

- 10 Other fragment outputs

- 11 GPU quirks

- 12 From picture to recipe

- 13 Capstone

- A Appendix

The whole course takes this planet apart: data → vertices → rasterization → fragments → output. In the last lesson you rewrite it yourself.

## Try it

- Look at the peaks and the water: the shading comes in bands, not a smooth gradient

- Start from any chapter in the contents; you can always come back
